'''Shmaryahu Hoz''' ({{Langx|he|שמריהו הוז}}; born 1945) is a Professor Emeritus specializing in [[physical organic chemistry]] and [[Computational chemistry|computational nanotechnology]].

==Biography==
Shmaryahu Hoz was born in Jerusalem in 1945.  He received a B.Sc. in Chemistry and Physics and an M.Sc. in Chemistry from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem|Hebrew University]]. He received his Ph.D. in Chemistry from [[Bar Ilan University]] and did post-doctoral studies at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]] with Prof. [[Joseph F. Bunnett]].
He joined the Chemistry Department at Bar Ilan University in 1975. His major research areas are: [[physical organic chemistry]], the chemistry of [[Samarium(II) iodide|SmI<sub>2</sub>]], [[Computational chemistry|computational nanotechnology]] and the effects of electric fields on structure and reactivity.<ref>[http://ch.biu.ac.il/hoz Hoz's page at Bar Ilan Chemistry depertmant]</ref>

==Administrative activities==
Professor Hoz has held several administrative positions at [[Bar Ilan University]]. He served as the Head of the Department of Chemistry and subsequently as Vice President for Research of the University.<ref>[http://research.biu.ac.il/content/about-us Bar-Ilan University (BIU) Research Authority]</ref> In his capacity as a VPR, he established the brain research center<ref>[http://www.gondabrain.biu.ac.il/ Gonda (Goldschmied) Multidisciplinary Brain Research Center at Bar-Ilan University]</ref> and set in place the foundations for the School of Engineering.<ref>[http://engineering.biu.ac.il/en Bar Ilan's Faculty of Electrical and Computer Engineering]</ref> For many years, Professor Hoz was in charge of the parliamentary aspects of the Board of Trustees of the University and headed the By-Laws Committee of the Senate of the University.

He currently serves as senior advisor to the university president and the head of the [[Bar Ilan Responsa Project|Responsa Project]].

==Scientific activities==
His major scientific achievements are: the discovery of the catalytic effect of fluoride ion;<ref>''Synthesis'' '''1975''', ''162'', 
[[doi:10.1055/s-1975-23689]]</ref> the discovery of the zwitterionic [[bicyclobutane]];<ref>''J. Am. Chem. Soc.'' '''1983''', ''105 (26)'', ''7685–7690'',
